title: rape-sentencing-guideline.pdf — section 5
text:
1 Whether a position of trust or authority exists at the time of the offence is for the court to assess, and it is not
possible to provide a complete list of such situations. Examples may include relationships such as teacher and
student, employer and employee, or carer and dependant, including where this relationship is a familia l one. It may
also include situations where there is no ongoing relationship or where the position of trust or authority is temporary,
such as childcare, or a taxi driver and a passenger.

2 Whether a victim is vulnerable at the time of the offence is for the court to assess, and it is not possible to provide a
complete list of such instances. It may include, for example, vulnerability of a continuing nature such as physical and
mental conditions or impairments, or of a temporary nature such as sleep or unconsciousness.

• Use of threats or coercion to facilitate the offence

Level B

limited to those listed above) not present
Harm
Level 1
• The extreme nature of, or the extreme impact caused by, one or more level 2 features or
other features of harm may elevate an offence to level 1
Level 2
• Severe psychological or physical harm or trauma4
• Additional degradation or humiliation
• Prolonged or sustained incident
• Pregnancy, and any consequences, as a result of the offence
• Sexually transmitted infection as a result of the offence
• Public or private sharing of any recording3 of the commission of the offence
Level 3
• Psychological or physical harm or trauma4
